title: Chemical Bonding I (Ionic & Covalent) - Chemistry - Lewis Structures
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the total number of valence electrons available for the Lewis structure of the carbonate ion, $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$?
questions.explain: C (Group 14) has 4 valence electrons. O (Group 16) has 6. The -2 charge adds 2 electrons. Total $= 4 + (3 \times 6) + 2 = 24$ electrons.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which element corresponds to the Lewis symbol $\cdot \dot{\text{X}} \cdot$ (3 single dots around the symbol)?
questions.explain: Aluminum is in Group 13 and has 3 valence electrons, represented as three dots in a Lewis symbol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the correct Lewis structure for Nitrogen gas ($\text{N}_2$), how many bonds connect the two nitrogen atoms?
questions.explain: Nitrogen has 5 valence electrons. To complete the octet for both atoms, they share 3 pairs of electrons, forming a triple bond.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following molecules violates the octet rule by having an incomplete octet?
questions.explain: Boron in $\text{BF}_3$ only has 6 valence electrons around it (3 bonds, 0 lone pairs). It is a classic example of an incomplete octet.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which molecule contains an 'expanded octet' (more than 8 electrons around the central atom)?
questions.explain: Sulfur in $\text{SF}_6$ is bonded to 6 fluorine atoms, resulting in 12 electrons around the central sulfur. This is possible because sulfur is in period 3 and has access to d-orbitals.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Identify the molecule that is an 'odd-electron' species (free radical).
questions.explain: Nitrogen monoxide (NO) has $5 + 6 = 11$ valence electrons. Being an odd number, it is impossible to pair all electrons, leaving one unpaired.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Draw (mentally) the Lewis structure for carbon dioxide, $\text{CO}_2$. What is the bonding arrangement?
options: O-C-O with single bonds and lone pairs on C.
O\equivC-O with a triple and single bond.
questions.explain: Carbon needs 4 bonds to complete its octet. Oxygen needs 2. The structure O=C=O satisfies the octet rule for all atoms with minimal formal charge.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which concept explains why the actual bonds in the ozone molecule ($\text{O}_3$) are identical in length, rather than one single and one double bond?
questions.explain: Resonance describes structures that cannot be represented by a single Lewis structure. In ozone, the actual structure is a hybrid of two resonance forms, making the bond lengths equal (intermediate between single and double).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How many resonance structures can be drawn for the nitrate ion ($\text{NO}_3^-$)?
questions.explain: Nitrate has one double bond and two single bonds in its Lewis structure. The double bond can be placed on any of the three oxygens, resulting in 3 equivalent resonance structures.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the Lewis structure for the hydronium ion ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$), how many lone pairs are on the oxygen atom?
questions.explain: Oxygen has 6 valence electrons. In $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$, 3 are used for bonding with H, and 1 electron is lost due to the + charge. Remaining: $6 - 3 - 1 = 2$ electrons, which form 1 lone pair.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following describes a 'Coordinate Covalent Bond' (or Dative Bond)?
options: A bond where electrons are transferred completely.
A bond where one atom provides both electrons for the shared pair.
A bond formed by the overlap of s-orbitals only.
A bond that is strictly magnetic in nature.
questions.explain: A coordinate covalent bond occurs when one atom donates a lone pair to form a bond with another atom (e.g., $\text{NH}_3$ bonding to $H^+$ to form $\text{NH}_4^+$).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the bond order of the carbon-oxygen bonds in the carbonate ion ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$)?
questions.explain: Carbonate has 3 resonance structures sharing 4 bonds (1 double, 2 single) across 3 positions. Bond order = Total Bonds / Number of positions = $4/3 \approx 1.33$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Based on Lewis structures, which molecule has the shortest carbon-carbon bond?
options: They are all the same length.
questions.explain: Ethyne has a carbon-carbon triple bond, Ethene has a double bond, and Ethane has a single bond. Triple bonds are the strongest and shortest.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Determine the number of lone pairs on the central atom of Xenon Difluoride ($\text{XeF}_2$).
questions.explain: Xe has 8 valence e-. Two form bonds with F. Remaining e- = $8 - 2 = 6$. These 6 electrons form 3 lone pairs.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explain: Isoelectronic means having the same number of valence electrons and structure. $\text{CO}_2$ has 16 valence e-. $\text{N}_3^-$ (Azide) has $5 \times 3 + 1 = 16$ valence e- and a similar linear structure.
questions.subject: Chemistry
